# `aitbc wallet inspect`

Print public metadata from a wallet file without decrypting it. Reads the JSON directly and only ever returns fields on a public allowlist — private_key, seed/mnemonic material, and any unknown field are refused. Only scalar values are printed: a public field holding a dict or list (e.g. `encrypted` as a crypto object in some keystore formats) is refused rather than dumped. Works on encrypted wallets without a password.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc wallet inspect [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--path` | text | — | yes | Path to the wallet JSON file |
| `--field` | text | — | no | Print a single public field (e.g. address) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc wallet inspect --path <wallet_file>
```
